message.content:
The three most significant schisms in Christian history are: | # | Schism | Approximate Year | Key Causes & Consequences | |---|--------|------------------|---------------------------| | 1 | **Great Schism (East–West Schism)** | 1054 | • Doctrinal differences (e.g., the Filioque clause, papal primacy).
• Cultural and political tensions between the Latin West and Greek East.
• Resulted in the permanent split between the Roman Catholic Church and the Eastern Orthodox Churches. | | 2 | **Protestant Reformation** | 1517–1648 | • Martin Luther’s 95 Theses challenged papal authority and church practices.
• Spread of reformist ideas led to the creation of numerous Protestant denominations (Lutheran, Calvinist, Anglican, etc.).
• Triggered religious wars, reforms in church governance, and a lasting diversification of Christian practice. | | 3 | **East–West Schism of 1965 (Ecumenical Dialogue)** | 1965 | • While not a “schism” in the traditional sense, the 1965 *Ecumenical Dialogue* between the Roman Catholic and Eastern Orthodox churches marked a formal attempt to heal the 1054 split.
• It was a significant moment of theological conversation and mutual recognition, though full reunification has not yet been achieved. | These events are often cited as the pivotal moments that shaped the major branches of Christianity and continue to influence inter‑church relations today.
